definition.def: If someone makes a discovery, they become aware of something that they did not know about before.
examples: I felt I'd made an incredible discovery.
...the discovery that both his wife and son are HIV positive.

definition.def: If someone makes a discovery, they are the first person to find or become aware of a place, substance, or scientific fact that no one knew about before.
examples: In that year, two momentous discoveries were made.
...the discovery of the ozone hole over the South Pole.
The fascination of discovery has never left him.

definition.def: If someone makes a discovery, they recognize that an actor, musician, or other performer who is not well-known has talent.
examples: His job is the discovery and promotion of new artists.

definition.def: When the discovery of people or objects happens, someone finds them, either by accident or as a result of looking for them.
examples: ...the discovery and destruction by soldiers of millions of marijuana plants. [+ of]

examples.sentence: The technique became more efficient after the discovery of iron, about 5000 years ago.
Fire-lighting was revolutionised by the discovery of phosphorus, isolated in 1669 by a German alchemist trying to transmute silver into gold.
An important archaeological discovery on the island of Efate in the Pacific archipelago of Vanuatu has revealed traces of an ancient seafaring people, the distant ancestors of today's Polynesians.

Then there's a sense of mounting discovery as he comes across great sweeps of terraces, then a mausoleum, followed by monumental staircases and, finally, the grand ceremonial buildings of Machu Picchu.
He spent the afternoon at the ruins noting down the dimensions of some of the buildings, then descended and rejoined his companions, to whom he seems to have said little about his discovery.
At this stage, Bingham didn't realise the extent or the importance of the site, nor did he realise what use he could make of the discovery.
However, soon after returning it occurred to him that he could make a name for himself from this discovery.
Until this discovery, the lynx - a large spotted cat with tasselled ears - was presumed to have died out in Britain at least 6,000 years ago, before the inhabitants of these islands took up farming.
Another discovery is that oxytocin's effects vary depending on who we are interacting with.
Laboratory-based drug discovery has achieved varying levels of success, something which has now prompted the development of new approaches focusing once again on natural products.
